# 1. Preparation

## Load packages

```{r}
#| label: load-packages-preparation
#| message: false
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(VisiumIO)
library(arrow)
library(qs2)
library(ggspavis)
library(patchwork)
library(dplyr)
library(arrow)
library(scuttle)
library(HDF5Array)
```

## Load Data

My data is stored in the following path. Please change the path accordingly.
```{r}
#| label: define-path
data_path <- "/home/kim/workspace/spatial_transcriptomics/data"
```

```{r}
#| label: define-data-path
visium_data_path <- file.path(data_path, "raw_colon_cancer")
hdf_data_path <- file.path(data_path, "hdf5_colon_cancer")
```

Visium HD spots are arranged as 2 × 2 µm squares. Space Ranger outputs data at three bin sizes: 2 µm, 8 µm, and 16 µm. Smaller bin sizes provide higher spatial resolution but result in greater data sparsity. In this tutorial, we use a bin size of 16 µm.

```{r}
#| label: import-data
spe <- TENxVisiumHD(
  spacerangerOut = visium_data_path,
  processing = "filtered",
  format = "h5",
  images = "lowres",
  bin_size = "016"
) |>
  import()
```

## Taking a peek at the data

```{r}
#| label: data-dimensions
dim(spe)
```

The dataset contains 127,809 spots and 18,085 genes.

Because *SpatialExperiment* is an extension of *SingleCellExperiment*, it uses a similar data structure: the count matrix is organized with genes as rows and spots as columns. If you are more familiar with Python’s *AnnData* and *scanpy*, note that this orientation is the transpose of what you may expect.

![](https://github.com/drighelli/SpatialExperiment/raw/devel/vignettes/SPE.png)

Metadata for spots and genes can be accessed using `colData(spe)` and `rowData(spe)`, respectively.

```{r}
#| label: spot-metadata
# Spot metadata
head(colData(spe))
```

```{r}
#| label: gene-metadata
# Gene metadata
head(rowData(spe))
```

Since the current row names are Ensembl ID, we update them to gene symbols for easier downstream analysis.

```{r}
#| label: update-rownames
rownames(spe) <- uniquifyFeatureNames(
  ID = rowData(spe)$ID,
  names = rowData(spe)$Symbol
)
```

The count matrix itself can be accessed using `counts(spe)`.
```{r}
#| label: count-matrix
head(counts(spe))
```

One of the data specific to spatial transcriptomics is the spatial coordinates of each spot, which can be accessed using `spatialCoords(spe)`.
```{r}
#| label: spatial-coordinates
head(spatialCoords(spe))
```

We can also visualize the spatial distribution of spots on the tissue slide using the `plotVisium()` function from the *ggspavis* package.
```{r}
#| label: plot-image
plotVisium(spe)
```

Based on the plot, we can see the tissue section and the spots that map to the tissue. It seems that the data is already filtered to retain only spots that map to the tissue. We can confirm this by checking the `in_tissue` column in the `colData(spe)`.
```{r}
#| label: check-in-tissue
table(spe$in_tissue)
```

We can also visualize the expression of a specific gene on the tissue slide. For example, we can visualize the expression of the gene `PIGR`.
```{r}
#| label: plot-gene-expression
plotVisium(
  spe,
  annotate = "PIGR",
  assay = "counts",
  point_size = 1,
  point_shape = 22
)
```

## Subsetting the data

Since the dataset is large, we will subset a smaller region for faster processing. To decide which region to subset, we zoom in on the tissue section where the spots are mapped using `zoom = TRUE` option. Also, we show the axes using `show_axes = TRUE` option to help us decide the bounding box coordinates.
```{r}
#| label: plot-zoomed
plotVisium(spe, spots = FALSE, zoom = TRUE, show_axes = TRUE)
```

The x and y axes values denotes `scalefactor` * `spatialCoords`. From the plot, we will subset the bounding box with the following coordinates:

- xmin: 70
- ymin: 200
- xsize: 60
- ysize: 60

```{r}
#| label: subset-data
bb_xmin <- 70
bb_ymin <- 200
bb_xsize <- 60
bb_ysize <- 60

getSubsetMask <- function(spe, xmin, ymin, xsize, ysize) {
  mask <-
    spatialCoords(spe)[, 1] * scaleFactors(spe) > xmin &
    spatialCoords(spe)[, 1] * scaleFactors(spe) < (xmin + xsize) &
    spatialCoords(spe)[, 2] * scaleFactors(spe) > ymin &
    spatialCoords(spe)[, 2] * scaleFactors(spe) < (ymin + ysize)
  return(mask)
}

spe <- spe[, getSubsetMask(spe, bb_xmin, bb_ymin, bb_xsize, bb_ysize)]
dim(spe)
```

After subsetting, there are 14,207 spots remaining. We can also visualize the subsetted region

```{r}
#| label: plot-subsetted
plotVisium(spe, spots = TRUE)
```

## Save the subsetted data
```{r}
#| label: save-subsetted
saveHDF5SummarizedExperiment(
  spe,
  dir = hdf_data_path,
  prefix = "01_subsetted_",
  replace = TRUE,
  chunkdim = NULL,
  level = NULL,
  as.sparse = NA,
  verbose = NA
)
```
